scores.notes: The side edges are painted all the way out: trees, grass and pale but tinted sky, with no white band or vignette. I followed scorer B. The item stays flawed because both scorers agreed on the glyph in the Hatter's hatband.

The pipe hangs in the air against Holmes's coat at chest level (centre right). Both hands are on the desk with the pen, and nothing holds the pipe. I followed scorer B; agreed lettering and likeness faults also stand.

A looped, signature-like scrawl that reads as 'Ob3' sits in the ochre foliage at the left edge (about x45,y230), so lettering is yes. The top-left sky is near-bare cream paper, which this style accepts. I followed scorer B on both.

The flagstone wash breaks into bare pale paper at the left edge of the bottom-left corner and along the bottom-right corner. This style accepts that. I followed scorer B; the item stays flawed because both scorers agreed on the duplicated lens.

David strides toward the lower left, away from Goliath, looking down into his bag. The plan asks for him to advance on the Philistine. Goliath stands mid-valley at the same scale as the soldiers, not towering. I followed scorer B.

The stone-wall wash fades to pale bare paper in the top-left corner above the arch, which this style accepts. I followed scorer B; the item stays flawed because both scorers agreed on the 'K' index and the scribbled papers.

The Queen copies the animated-film design: black hair in a bun, a tiny crown, a tall flared stand-up collar and a red gown with heart trim. That breaks the rule against costumes from adaptations. This is a borrowed costume, not a real person's likeness. I followed scorer A.

Contrast-stretched, the titulus (top centre, about 30px wide) shows only mottled wood with no glyph shapes. The Dome-of-the-Rock-like blue dome on the left skyline is an anachronism, not an internal contradiction of pose, object or place. I followed scorer B; the operator may still want to note the anachronism.

Small patches of bare cream paper show at the left edge of the bottom-left rocks and along the bottom and right edges of the bottom-right waves. This style accepts that, so the item stays acceptable. I followed scorer A.

The teacups and sugar bowl carry letter-shaped painted marks that read as 'CUY', 'CUD' and 'JUE', and a plate rim shows 'oim'-like squiggles (table centre and right). These read as glyph-like inscriptions. I followed scorer B.

The bottom-left floor and the other corners are fully washed in grey and brown, and the top-right light is painted pale blue sky. There is no bare band. I followed scorer B; the item stays flawed because both scorers agreed on the 'DRINK ME' tag.
Bare cream paper shows in the top-left corner beside the cloud and in small white patches at the right edge, above the tent and at lower right. This style accepts that. I followed scorer A.

Egyptian chariots and horsemen fill the seabed between two towering walls of water under dark cloud. Because they move toward the viewer, the view reads as from the far shore, and the pursuit still reads. The Israelites are not distinguishable, but that is a secondary element. I followed scorer A.

Jerusalem appears twice: a walled hill city with its own temple platform on the left, and a second walled fortress topped by another temple on the right. That gives two contradictory temples. I followed scorer A.

At lower right, a plank deck or pier with coiled rope and net sits outside the hull, alongside a boat that is otherwise tossed in open water with waves beyond. That places the boat in two settings at once. I followed scorer A.

David faces armoured Goliath across the brook with staff, bag and a smooth stone in hand, and the shield bearers and soldiers are on the slope. The missing sling is a minor prop gap, and the advance on Goliath reads. I followed scorer B.

About nine white-bearded elders and other men sit and stand across the whole right third. They are prominent, and they are too old to be Jesse's sons. The selection names only Jesse, three sons, Samuel and David. I followed scorer A.

Four men already stand waiting beyond the fire at right; the plan has the disciples arrive from the boat. One of them is long-haired and centre-parted in the conventional Jesus type, and Jesus was not selected. I followed scorer A.

In the drinking crowd at lower right, a man's head and arm rise straight out of a donkey's withers with no torso. Nearby, a drinker's face in the water shares the yellow-robed body of the bearded man above him. Both are merged bodies. I followed scorer B.

The seated, moustached Watson (right) closely matches Martin Freeman's Victorian-era screen Watson: swept short hair, knitted upturned brows, rounded nose and face shape. It is recognisable as a screen likeness. I followed scorer A, with moderate confidence.
The ground wash stops short of the bottom-left corner, leaving bare white paper along the bottom edge. This style accepts that. I followed scorer B.

The arch soldiers carry only club and spade pips, which the card-courtier rule asks for, and no legible indices or letters. The top-right sky is near-bare cream paper, which this style accepts. I followed scorer B on both; the item stays flawed because both scorers agreed on the whole-bodied Cat and the three-legged flamingo.

Jesus stands inside the tomb beside the rolled stone, and the bound Lazarus already stands outside among the crowd. Lazarus is not shown emerging at the threshold as Jesus calls him forth. I followed scorer B.
Holmes (left, in profile with the lens) has Peter Cushing's gaunt long face, receding swept-back hair and deep cheek lines. It is the same face both scorers agreed on in i103. I followed scorer A.
Holmes holding the lantern (centre) has a widow's-peak receding hairline, slicked-back hair, hollow cheeks and a long jaw. That is a close Peter Cushing likeness. I followed scorer A.

The seraphim are conventional robed human angels with four wings and bare, uncovered feet. They are not the six-winged creatures covering face and feet that the text describes. That breaks the rule that visionary creatures follow the text. I followed scorer A.

Every listed fault is an agreed 'no'. Below the central fiery wheel there is a faint T-shaped shaft of light, but at normal viewing it reads as a light beam, with no head, face or limbs. I followed scorer B.

Alice pausing with the flamingo, the hedgehogs crawling over the furrows and the Queen stamping and shouting are all shown on the croquet lawn. The card soldiers walking hand in hand instead of forming arches is a secondary-element miss. I followed scorer B; the item stays flawed because both scorers agreed on lettering and the film costume.
Holmes on the bed has the same gaunt, receding, swept-back Peter Cushing face seen in i103, i179 and i182: long nose, hollow cheeks, deep lines. I followed scorer A.
